source.episode_title: Could Ye Not Watch One Hour
source.anchor_kjv: And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?
source.thread: Jesus asked three fishermen to watch one hour and they slept - his mercy diagnoses the weak flesh he then died for
source.hook_line: Jesus asked three fishermen for one thing.
source.spoken_script: Jesus asked three fishermen for one thing. They failed inside an hour. Gethsemane. The night before the cross. tarry ye here, and watch with me. Then he stepped away to pray. O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour? Not a curse. A diagnosis full of mercy. Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. He returned to the same prayer. The cup he asked to pass, he drank. On the cross. For you. So bring him the weak flesh he already knows. When you cannot watch, pray anyway. He is watching. He watched that hour alone. Now no hour of yours is watched alone.

platforms.title: Could Ye Not Watch With Me One Hour? Gethsemane, Matthew 26:40
platforms.description:
Matthew 26:40 - in Gethsemane, the night before the cross, Jesus asked three fishermen for one small thing: tarry ye here, and watch with me. Inside an hour he found them asleep.

"And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?" (Matthew 26:40, KJV)

His question was not a curse - it was a diagnosis full of mercy: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. Then he returned to the same prayer, and the cup he asked to pass, he drank. On the cross. For you.

This episode of Questions Jesus Asked walks through the Gethsemane account in the King James Version, panel by panel, in hand-inked comic art: the garden at night, the cup in the moonlight, the sleeping disciples, and the mercy in the question Jesus asked them.

He watched that hour alone. Now no hour of yours is watched alone. Bring Jesus the weak flesh he already knows - when you cannot watch, pray anyway.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS

- youtube_long: "This episode ... walks through the Gethsemane account ... panel by panel" - this block describes a long-form deep-dive but the source video is a 60-second short. The pack for a short only ships youtube_short/tiktok/facebook/instagram, so this block is unused today; if it is ever pasted for a long upload, rewrite it against the actual long video first. Not blocking for this short's pack.
- youtube_short title "Jesus Asked Three Fishermen for One Thing. They Failed in an Hour." - honest to the narration ("They failed inside an hour"), no curiosity-gap lie. Keep.
- Verse check: the Matthew 26:40 quote in youtube_short and facebook matches the supplied KJV string character-for-character, including "What, could ye not watch with me one hour?". PASS.
- Doctrine: "not a curse, a diagnosis full of mercy" and "no hour of yours is watched alone" are the video's own landing lines - no overclaim, no fear/gain-loss framing. The CTA points to Jesus. PASS.
- TikTok/Instagram: first line is the hook, no URLs, caption under budget. PASS.
- Minor: "ONE thing" in all-caps on TikTok/IG reads as emphasis, not shouting - acceptable, but do not stack more caps.
